title.en: Language work for I Too Had a Dream: synonyms, expressions, dashes, stress and a letter of thanks

text.en: Dr Verghese Kurien's story carries phrases about humility and effort. This lesson looks at words that mean almost the same, expressions about character, two kinds of dash, how stress changes a word from a noun to a verb, and how to write a letter of thanks.

keepEnglishTerms: in all humility, hold their heads high, to be quite honest
to the best of your ability, in awe, deep down

text.en:
Synonyms are words with nearly the same meaning. Magnificent is splendid, fleeting is momentary, instant is swift, core is essential, valuable is useful, and abiding is lifelong. A synonym must also fit the sentence.
In all humility means being humble with no feeling of self-importance. To hold their heads high is to be confident and have a positive feeling. To be quite honest is to speak in a truthful way.
To the best of your ability means using all your skills, talents and knowledge. Looked at in awe means observed with great respect and wonder, and somewhere deep down means in the innermost part of the self.
The en dash is the shorter dash and shows a span or range, as in train operates June–September, refer to pages 50–75 and India won the series 2–1.
The em dash is the longer dash. It adds extra information or shows a change in thought, as in 'The exhibition—held in the main hall—features local artists'. Do not put spaces around a dash and do not overuse it.
Some words change stress when they change part of speech. A noun usually has the stress on the first syllable, PREsent, and a verb on the second, preSENT. In the same way PROduce is a noun and proDUCE a verb, CONtract is a noun and conTRACT a verb, and PROject is a noun and proJECT a verb.
A letter of thanks to grandparents should thank them for the lessons and stories they shared, say how their wisdom has shaped your values and behaviour, and share how their actions inspire you to do something good for society.

problem.en: Insert the right dash: (a) The conference will be held from March 15 ___ March 20. (b) The artist ___ known for her vibrant paintings ___ will show her work in Guwahati. Then mark the stress in the noun and verb forms of 'project'.

text.en: (a) March 15–March 20 uses an en dash because it shows a range of dates.

why.en: A range uses the en dash.

text.en: (b) The artist—known for her vibrant paintings—will show her work in Guwahati uses em dashes to add extra information.

why.en: Extra information inside a sentence uses the em dash.

text.en: The noun is PROject with stress on the first syllable and the verb is proJECT with stress on the second.

why.en: Noun: first syllable; verb: second syllable.

prompt.en: Explain the difference between an en dash and an em dash with one example each, and say which syllable is stressed in the verb 'present'.

requiredIdeas.en: en dash: a range such as June–September
em dash: extra information or a change in thought
The verb preSENT has stress on the second syllable

commonMisconceptions.en: Using only a hyphen for ranges

points.en: En dash shows a range; em dash adds extra information.
Noun stress is on the first syllable and verb stress on the second: PRESent/preSENT.
